This study presents a novel time-varying regression model called TV-PAR, aiming to analyze and forecast count-based data. The TV-PAR model differs from traditional count models as it allows for changes in conditional mean and variance over time, making it suitable for data with shifting patterns. We develop an estimation method for the TV-PAR model, utilizing a semi-parametric approach to handle changing patterns and a local least squares method to estimate parameters. We then conduct a simulation study to evaluate the performance of our estimation procedure, demonstrating its effectiveness in various scenarios. Additionally, we apply the TV-PAR model to real-world data sets, analyzing the factors influencing hospital infections and newspaper article frequencies, and forecasting future counts based on our analyses. The code used in this study is available for public use.

Numerous numerical simulations relying on molecular dynamics or Monte Carlo methods execute stochastic moves to explore configuration space. These simulations often employ Langevin Dynamics, which is a type of stochastic numerical integration that resembles molecular dynamics and evolves systems through a series of tiny time-step steps. Although straightforward to implement, the current research reveals that Langevin Dynamics might not always yield the most efficient configuration exploration, which is critical for applications like free energy calculations and biomolecular simulations. In this study, we introduce an enhanced Langevin Dynamics (eLD) algorithm that exploits existing force data to facilitate more substantial stochastic moves, resulting in more effective configuration exploration with minimal computational expense. Compared to standard Langevin Dynamics, eLD leads to a 10 times increase in accepted move sizes on average, as well as significantly improved simulation efficiency in both isolated system and constant temperature/pressure ensemble simulations. Moreover, eLD enables simulations to exit local conformational traps more easily, allowing for the accurate calculation of absolute free energies with reduced error. The code for the enhanced Langevin Dynamics is available on GitHub at https://github.com/CompChemGroup/UeLD. Currently, the eLD code is integrated into LAMMPS through an add-on package called ueld. Users can also utilize the eLD code within the GROMACS simulation package by compiling it from source. The paper's supplementary materials include additional information on the eLD code's implementation, as well as further simulation details.
